newsitem.title: USA: LILCO has power dip from NY substation fire.
newsitem.headline: LILCO has power dip from NY substation fire.

text.p: Long Island Lighting Co (LILCO) said it experienced a brief power dip early Wednesday after a fire broke out at a ConEd substation in nearby Yonkers, N.Y.
"It was a flicker. It was a few seconds, and it came back on," said a LILCO spokeswoman, adding the outage affected customers in Nassau County and western Suffolk County.

Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc (ConEd), which operates the Sprain Brook power substation, blamed the fire for a major power dip in New York City and Westchester County, just north of the city.
The New York Power Pool, which oversees the state's transmission system, said the fire shut six high-voltage transmission lines.
One of those lines, rated at 345 kilovolts, ties into a substation in Garden City, Long Island and was likely the cause of the power dip in LILCO's service territory.
LILCO provides electric service to one million customers on Long Island.
